[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like TSLA on 2026-09-18, the realised 20-session returns centred on a median of 2.96%, with 68% of those analogs finishing above zero. The single number to anchor on is that median: it describes what happened next in the closest matches, not a forecast for the coming month.

[state]
The retrieval engine pulled these 50 analogs because TSLA's current state combines several distinctive features. The 5d/20d volatility ratio is compressed at 0.489 (z-score -1.217), while 20-session realised volatility remains elevated at 48.97% (z-score 0.983). Dollar volume is thin, with a 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score of -1.558 (used as -1.026). WTI crude has surged 19.24% over 20 days (z-score 1.124), and the stock sits 26.98% below its 52-week high with a 14.35% drawdown from its 60-session peak. Earnings are capped at 45 days away. These features pull in a mix of names across Technology (12 analogs), China ADR (7), Consumer Disc. (5), and ETF China (8), heavily concentrated in recent sessions (20 from 2025, 12 from 2026). The macro backdrop shows a VIX level of 15.44, a 10y-2y Treasury slope of 0.25, and a 90-day Fed funds target change of 0.25 bp. Market sentiment registers in the Greed band at a value of 70. Headlines framing the current session include CNBC Markets noting "Stock futures are flat as investors grapple with higher yields, await Fed minutes" and "Surging Treasury yields don’t signal a U.S. 'fiscal apocalypse' — yet." Derivatives positioning data is unavailable on this card.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs, the mean 20-session forward return was 2.39% and the median was 2.96%, with a standard deviation of 6.9%. The distribution carries a slight negative skew of -0.288. The 10th percentile outcome was -8.68% and the 90th percentile was 10.51%. In 32% of the retrieved episodes, the 20-session return finished below zero. The bad tail is dominated by specific sessions: Li Auto (LI) on 2025-09-22 realised -11.47% with a max adverse excursion of -13.16%, and Boeing (BA) on 2021-08-04 realised -3.76% after dropping -6.92% intra-horizon. On the upside, Schlumberger (SLB) on 2026-08-04 returned 12.48%, Nike (NKE) on 2023-10-10 returned 12.03%, and the single TSLA match from 2025-08-07 returned 8.87%.

[tails]
Path risk matters more than the endpoint. The median maximum adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -3.53%, meaning half the time the position drew down more than that before the 20 sessions ended. The 10th percentile of max adverse excursion reached -10.99%. In 40% of the analogs, the path breached a 5% drawdown at some point during the 20 sessions. A 10% drawdown was breached in 14% of the episodes. No analog in the set breached a 15% or 20% drawdown. The median max favourable excursion was 6.73%, yielding a reward-to-risk ratio of 1.91 based on the medians.

[stress]
The baseline median return of 2.96% deteriorates materially under several stress scenarios. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario produced a median forward return of -7.83% across 50 analogs, a delta of -10.79% versus baseline, with a 74% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare yielded a median of -6.29% (delta -9.25%) across 50 analogs, with a 50% probability of a 10% drawdown breach; caveat: it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash showed a median of -3.2% (delta -6.16%) across 48 analogs, with a 72.9% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns. The 2025-04 tariff shock produced a median of -0.86% (delta -3.82%) across 26 analogs, with a 61.5% probability of a 10% drawdown breach; caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The +2 sigma VIX spike scenario gave a median of -2.28% (delta -5.24%) across 50 analogs, with a 36% probability of a 10% drawdown breach; caveat: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. The earnings release day scenario resulted in a median of -1.18% (delta -4.14%) across 50 analogs, with a 48% probability of a 10% drawdown breach; caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text
